title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participates in Vijaya Dashami celebrations in Delhi
subtitle:
Vijaya Dashami celebrates the victory of good over evil; It reminds us of the enduring strength of truth and righteousness: PM

For us, this is not merely a festival; this is the life energy of India: PM

Lord Ram has given us such ideals which are incomparable in the history of humanity: PM

We have to keep the service of the poor and the deprived paramount: PM

When we stand with truth and humanity, then in the end, victory is ours: PM

The vision of ‘Ram Se Rashtra’ and ‘Dev Se Desh’ that we have conceived, we will definitely fulfill it: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 OCT 2026 8:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in Vijaya Dashami celebrations in Delhi.
Addressing the Vijayadashami celebrations at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, the Prime Minister
commenced his address by extending his warmest festive wishes to the entire nation on the auspicious occasion. "I extend my heartfelt greetings of Vijayadashami to all the countrymen,” remarked Shri Modi.
Describing how every village and city across India is immersed in the staging of Ramlilas, the Prime Minister highlighted the tradition of keeping Lord Ram’s ideals alive, proclaiming the end of tyranny and terror, and upholding the victory of eternal truth over falsehood. He invited the gathering to join him in chanting praises to the deity as citizens nationwide celebrate the triumph of righteousness over unrighteousness. "For us, this is not merely a festival; this is the life energy of India,” asserted PM Modi.
Reflecting on the millennia-old devotion of India’s culture and ancestors toward Lord Shri Ram, the Prime Minister noted that this deep reverence extends far beyond his victory over the demon king Ravana. He emphasized that the enduring faith of the nation is anchored in the timeless values Lord Ram imparted to the world. "Lord Ram has given us such ideals which are incomparable in the history of humanity,” observed Shri Modi.
Recalling the immense hardships Lord Shri Ram faced without ever forsaking truth and morality, the Prime Minister quoted the Sanskrit verse to illustrate his equanimity during both his royal coronation and his forest exile. He highlighted how Lord Ram upheld righteousness through every crisis, embraced Nishadraj, and honored Mother Shabari during his time in the forest. "He established benchmarks of mercy, compassion, love, and harmony,” remarked PM Modi.
Detailing the establishment of Ramrajya upon Lord Ram's return as the King of Ayodhya, the Prime Minister described it as the ultimate benchmark of non-discriminatory governance where everyone receives justice and equal opportunity, and where power serves public welfare rather than authority, as immortalized in Goswami Tulsidas’s verse “Daihik Daivik Bhautik Tapa, Ram Raj Nahin Kahuhi Byapa.” He urged the administration to follow these ideals of Maryada Purushottam by treating the public as divine under the mantra of Nagrik Devo Bhava. "We have to keep the service of the poor and the deprived paramount,” asserted Shri Modi.
Drawing profound lessons of self-reliance from Lord Ram’s journey across the ocean to Lanka, the Prime Minister explained that instead of relying on others during a crisis, Lord Ram awakened collective public participation (Janbhagidari) and pooled available resources to achieve the impossible through faith, capability, and unwavering resolve. He called upon citizens to adopt this fundamental mantra of hard work and resourcefulness to fulfill public aspirations and achieve the goals of a Viksit Bharat and an Aatmanirbhar Bharat. "Lord Ram taught us that the difficulties on the path cannot stop our journey,” affirmed PM Modi.
Linking national progress to a strong sense of self-respect rooted in cultural heritage, the Prime Minister detailed the government's active campaign to preserve India's identity by repatriating over 650 ancient idols over the past 12 years. He also celebrated the growing global recognition of India's cultural centers, noting the inclusion of numerous domestic sites on the UNESCO World Heritage list and the inscription of Deepavali on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity list last year through the collective willpower of crores of Indians. "We have to continue working with this same dedication in the future,” noted Shri Modi.
Invoking the courageous spirit of Vijayadashami that guarantees triumph when standing with truth and humanity, the Prime Minister quoted the Vedic mantra “Samano Mantrah Samitih Samani” to urge all national institutions and political parties to unite in the national interest. He called upon citizens to adopt a 'Nation First' pledge to jointly identify and defeat the enemies of Maa Bharati, specifically forces that harm national honor, divide society, and harbor hatred toward Indian culture. "When we stand with truth and humanity, then in the end, victory is ours,” asserted PM Modi.
Concluding his address with deep conviction, the Prime Minister recalled the sacred resolutions taken during the Pran Pratishtha ceremony at the Ayodhya temple and extended his final Dussehra greetings alongside chants of Jai Siya Ram and Bharat Mata Ki Jai. He expressed absolute confidence in realizing the nation's spiritual and developmental vision. "The vision of ‘Ram Se Rashtra’ and ‘Dev Se Desh’ that we have conceived, we will definitely fulfill it,” affirmed Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of PM's address at the Vijaya Dashami celebrations in Delhi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 OCT 2026 7:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Victory to Lord Shri Ram!
Victory to Lord Shri Ram!
Victory to Lord Shri Ram!
On this sacred occasion of Vijayadashami, I bow at the feet of Lord Shri Ram, Mother Janaki, and Bajrang Bali. In this holy atmosphere, I extend my heartfelt greetings to all countrymen on Vijayadashami.
Friends,
Today, every corner of India is immersed in devotion to Lord Ram. Village after village, city after city, the nation is absorbed in the spirit of Ramleela. The staging of Ramleelas across the country, the tradition of keeping alive the ideals of Lord Shri Ram, the proclamation of the end of tyranny and terror, and the faith in the eternal victory of truth over falsehood, for us, this is not merely a festival. It is the life force of India. Therefore, today, when every citizen of the nation is proclaiming the victory of righteousness over unrighteousness, come, once again, repeat after me:
Victory to Lord Shri Ram!
Victory to Lord Shri Ram!
Victory to Lord Shri Ram!
Friends,
This nation, its culture, and its ancestors have worshipped Lord Shri Ram for thousands of years. This faith exists not only because Shri Ram brought an end to the demon king Ravana. This faith also exists because Lord Ram gave us ideals that are unparalleled in the history of humanity.
Friends,
Lord Shri Ram faced countless difficulties in his life, yet he never abandoned the path of truth and righteousness. Such was his character: "Prasannatam ya na gata abhishekatah tatha, na mamle vanavasa duhkhatoh." This means that Lord Ram neither became elated upon receiving the kingdom nor became distressed by the sorrow of exile in the forest. Despite enduring every adversity, he upheld righteousness and established truth. When Lord Ram went into the forest, he embraced Nishadraj and honoured Mother Shabari. He established the highest standards of compassion, kindness, love, and harmony. And when Lord Ram returned and became the king of Ayodhya, he established such a Ram Rajya that even today it is considered the benchmark of good governance. Ram Rajya means a system where there is no discrimination against anyone, where everyone receives justice, where everyone gets equal opportunities, where the purpose of power is not to rule but to serve the welfare of the people. That is why Goswami Tulsidas ji wrote: "Daihik daivik bhautik tapa, Ram raj nahin kahuhi vyapa." This is the ideal of Maryada Purushottam Lord Shri Ram. Therefore, we must always regard the people as divine and move forward with the mantra of Citizen First. We must place service to the poor and the deprived above everything else.
Friends,
We receive a very great lesson from the life of Lord Ram. No matter how great the crisis may be, no matter how difficult the challenge, we must not sit waiting for others. We must recognise our own strength. We must trust our own resources. We must turn our resolve into power. And we must find solutions through our own hard work. Lord Ram taught us that difficulties on the path cannot stop our journey. The ocean stood before him. Lanka was far away. But the resolve was unwavering. Therefore, Lord Ram awakened the collective strength of the people. He made public participation his support. He united the available resources. And he made a goal that seemed impossible. This is the fundamental mantra of success. Faith in our own strength. Confidence in our own capability. Proper utilisation of our own resources. And unwavering commitment to our goal. Today, we too must move forward with this same mantra. Before us stands the goal of a Developed India. Before us stands the goal of a Self-Reliant India. Through the power of the people and for the welfare of the people, we must fulfil every aspiration of our citizens. And for this too, we must draw inspiration from Lord Ram.
Friends,
A nation progresses only when it possesses self-respect. And heritage plays a very important role in this self-respect. Therefore, today the country is committed to preserving its heritage and identity. For centuries, our treasures were looted and taken abroad. But today, we are bringing those treasures back. In the past twelve years, more than six hundred and fifty ancient idols have been brought back to India. Similarly, India is giving new global recognition to its cultural centres. In recent years, many of our sites have been added to the UNESCO World Heritage List. Last year, even Diwali was included by UNESCO in the list of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. This is the result of the collective willpower of millions of Indians. We must continue to work with the same dedication.
Friends,
Vijayadashami is the festival of victory. It is the festival of triumph. This festival gives us the courage to believe that no matter how powerful the enemy may be, when we stand with truth and humanity, victory ultimately belongs to us. This spirit of Vijayadashami has always been India's guiding philosophy. Our sages inspired us: "Samano mantrah samitih samani, samanam manah saha chittamesham." This means that our thoughts should be united, our councils should be united, and all institutions of the nation, all political parties, should stand together in the national interest. We must move forward with this spirit. We must unite against the enemies of the nation. Those forces that attack the honour and dignity of the country, those who divide society, and those who harbour hatred towards our culture, are enemies of the nation. On this auspicious occasion of Vijayadashami, we must once again renew our resolve. We must identify the enemies of Mother India. We must defeat them. And, taking the pledge of Nation First, everyone must come together. I am confident that the vision we expressed during the Pran Pratishtha ceremony of the Ayodhya Temple, “From Ram to Nation” and “From Divinity to National Duty,” will certainly be fulfilled. I once again extend my heartfelt greetings to all countrymen on Dussehra.
Jai Siya Ram!
Jai Siya Ram!
Jai Siya Ram!
Bharat Mata Ki Jai!
Bharat Mata Ki Jai!
Thank you very much.

title: India’s Nuclear Programme Dedicated to Peaceful Purposes, Says Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh; Nuclear Energy to Power AI-Driven Future
subtitle:
Dr. Homi Bhabha’s vision continues to guide India’s peaceful nuclear journey as the country advances towards energy security and clean power: Dr. Jitendra Singh

“One has to be intelligent enough to use Artificial Intelligence”, Dr. Jitendra Singh stresses responsible, human-led use of AI across sectors

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has opened critical and sensitive sectors to non-government players, creating wider opportunities for private sector participation

India targets 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047 and Net Zero emissions by 2070, with nuclear energy set to meet growing demand for reliable, clean electricity: Dr. Jitendra Singh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 OCT 2026 2:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh has said that India’s nuclear programme is dedicated to peaceful purposes and not warfare, reaffirming the vision that has guided the country’s nuclear journey since its inception.
In an exclusive conversation on the sidelines of ‘Bloomberg Economy Forum 2026’, the Minister said nuclear energy would play an increasingly important role in meeting India’s future energy requirements, including the growing demand for reliable electricity to support Artificial Intelligence (AI) and data centres.
Recalling the vision of Dr. Homi Bhabha, the architect of India’s nuclear programme, Dr. Jitendra Singh said India had consistently pursued nuclear energy for peaceful applications and national development. The commitment to the peaceful use of nuclear technology, he said, remains central to the country’s approach as it expands its capabilities to meet emerging developmental and technological needs.
The Minister said India’s nuclear energy ambitions must be viewed in the context of its long-term development goals and clean energy commitments. With the country targeting 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047 and Net Zero emissions by 2070, nuclear energy is expected to complement other sources of power by providing a continuous and reliable supply of clean electricity.
Linking nuclear energy with the next phase of technological growth, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the expansion of Artificial Intelligence and data centres would require dependable sources of electricity capable of meeting their substantial and continuous energy needs. Nuclear energy, he said, would supplement India’s other energy programmes and contribute to meeting the power requirements of an increasingly technology-driven economy.
On the expanding role of Artificial Intelligence, the Minister said AI should be viewed as a tool applicable across sectors rather than as a domain in itself. From Space and life sciences to other areas of scientific and technological development, AI is set to become an increasingly necessary instrument. Emphasising the importance of human judgement in its application, he said, “One has to be intelligent enough to use Artificial Intelligence.”
Dr. Jitendra Singh said AI offers significant advantages across domains, but ensuring its optimal use without allowing it to be misused by individuals or other actors remains a key challenge. While regulations are in place, he said integrity at both the individual and national level is fundamental to ensuring that the technology is used responsibly. India, he added, has made appreciable efforts in this direction under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
The Minister also referred to the wider opening of critical and sensitive sectors to non-government players under the Modi Government. He said the approach has expanded the scope for private sector participation in areas that were traditionally more restricted, creating opportunities for industry to contribute to technological advancement, innovation and national development.
Dr. Jitendra Singh’s remarks bring together two important dimensions of India’s development trajectory: strengthening nuclear energy as a dependable source of clean power and harnessing emerging technologies such as AI through responsible, human-led application. As India advances towards its 2047 development goals and its 2070 Net Zero commitment, reliable energy infrastructure and wider participation in strategic sectors will remain important to sustaining the country’s technological and economic ambitions.

title: PM Modi-led Govt is striving to make India a nation that combines prosperity, knowledge and strength with a commitment to global peace & well-being of humanity: Raksha Mantri
date:

                20 OCT 2026 8:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
“Guided by the philosophy of
Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam
, India aspires to become a nation that combines prosperity, knowledge & strength with a commitment to global peace and the well-being of humanity,” said Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh while addressing the Indian diaspora in Dushanbe, Tajikistan on October 20, 2026. He emphasised that India’s economic transformation, reform-driven governance, technological advancement and growing global stature under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership are paving the way towards the realisation of this vision.
Highlighting India’s growth trajectory, Raksha Mantri stated that the country contributes more than 16 per cent to global economic growth and is growing at approximately 7.8 per cent, even as several major economies face a slowdown. Referring to the changing global trade landscape, the Raksha Mantri said that India has entered into Free Trade Agreements with 38 countries, opening new markets for Indian manufacturers and producers. He stated that the India-UK and India-EU trade agreements, which are expected to eliminate tariffs on 99 per cent of Indian exports to these markets, would strengthen the country’s trade prospects and global economic partnerships.
On the transformation in governance and policymaking over the last decade, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that India has moved from an era of ‘policy paralysis’ to a ‘reform express’ driven by a clear policy direction. “For us, reforms are not a compulsion; they are a conviction,” he said.
Raksha Mantri noted that the current account deficit, which exceeded four per cent of GDP 12-13 years ago, declined to 0.61 per cent in the previous financial year. India’s foreign exchange reserves have crossed US$700 billion, while the banking system is in its strongest-ever position, he added.
Highlighting India’s progress in defence manufacturing, Shri Rajnath Singh said that defence exports have reached a record Rs 38,424 crore, with defence production surging to Rs 1.80 lakh crore. He underlined that the number of start-ups has grown from a few hundred before 2014 to more than 2.5 lakh, and nearly half of these start-ups originate from smaller cities and towns, while more than 45 per cent have at least one woman director or partner. He said that affordable mobile data and wider connectivity have enabled more Indians to access opportunities, encouraging innovation, nurturing new talent and generating fresh solutions.
Raksha Mantri also highlighted the impact of inclusive development, stating that approximately 25 crore people have been lifted out of poverty over the past decade. He underscored the role of the JAM Trinity and Direct Benefit Transfer in delivering government assistance directly into beneficiaries’ bank accounts, reducing corruption and enhancing transparency and convenience.
Shri Rajnath Singh noted that India’s renewable energy capacity has increased from approximately 75 GW in 2014 to nearly 300 GW. title: 25th SCO Council of Heads of Government Meeting: Raksha Mantri calls for unified action to dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism

Connectivity must be based on consultation and respect for the sovereignty & territorial integrity of all countries: Shri Rajnath Singh

“SCO’s success lies in creating opportunities for youth, entrepreneurs, farmers & small businesses”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 OCT 2026 1:16PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called upon the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Member States to make concerted efforts to dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism, describing the menace as one of the gravest threats to peace and development. He was addressing the 25th Meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (CHG) of SCO in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 20, 2026.
“Terrorism results in the loss of innocent lives and disrupts investment & commerce. It radicalises societies and deprives youth of the opportunities they rightfully deserve. There can be no justification for terrorism, no double standards in addressing it, and no place for those who finance, support, or provide safe havens to terrorists,” said Raksha Mantri.
Shri Rajnath Singh recalled the deliberations at the SCO Summit in Bishkek in August-September 2026, when Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi underlined the need for concrete steps by the Organisation on issues related to security, connectivity, and opportunity. Raksha Mantri underscored India’s belief that economic engagement should be inclusive and mutually beneficial for all Member States. “India believes that the SCO must remain efficient and steadfast in its adherence to the principles of sovereign equality, consensus, and mutual respect. A greater number of institutions does not necessarily translate into greater achievements. New mechanisms should focus on clearly identified needs, avoid duplication, and prioritise delivering practical value to Member States,” he said.
Raksha Mantri emphasised the need for the SCO to build consensus and translate it into concrete action to address the uncertain global economic environment marked by geopolitical tensions, disruptions to trade and supply chains, concerns over energy and food security, and emerging technological divides. There is a need to strengthen resilient supply chains, facilitate trade and investment, and leverage technology to drive development, he said. Stressing that the benefits of economic cooperation must reach all sections of society, he reaffirmed India’s support for the adoption of an Action Plan for the Multilateral Trade and Economic Cooperation Programme for the period 2026-2030.
Shri Rajnath Singh welcomed the decisions taken at the SCO Summit in Bishkek to establish the Universal Centre in Tashkent and the Anti-Drug Centre in Dushanbe as permanent bodies of the Organisation. Their effectiveness, he said, would depend on efficient coordination and timely execution of tasks.
Underlining the importance of connectivity for shared prosperity, Raksha Mantri stated that India supports initiatives that link markets, facilitate trade and create new avenues for development. He said that initiatives such as the International North-South Transport Corridor and the Chabahar Port can contribute significantly to connecting Central Asia with broader markets.
Shri Rajnath Singh stressed that connectivity must be based on consultation and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries, adding that projects not founded on these principles will not be sustainable. He emphasised the need to move beyond physical connectivity by simplifying customs procedures, promoting digital documentation, improving logistics and adopting interoperable digital solutions to reduce the cost of doing business across the region.
Raksha Mantri highlighted the symposium on financing infrastructure projects in Central Asia, held in Mumbai earlier this month, and expressed gratitude to Central Asian countries and SCO partners for their active participation. He also acknowledged the organisation of the first-ever SCO Asian Economic Dialogue.
“Our success should be measured by the opportunities we create for youth, new markets we open for our entrepreneurs, technologies we make available to our farmers and small-scale business owners, and the connections we foster among societies,” said Shri Rajnath Singh.
Raksha Mantri asserted that India’s own development experience demonstrates the transformative potential of technology and innovation that drive growth and deliver solutions. He highlighted the country’s Digital Public Infrastructure, which has transformed public service delivery and enhanced financial inclusion. He added that India has built one of the world’s largest start-up ecosystems, and the nation’s emphasis on women-led development is rooted in the belief that women play a defining role in shaping the path of development.
Shri Rajnath Singh underlined that India’s global initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance and the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure contribute to affordable clean energy & climate-resilient development. He added that Mission LiFE promotes sustainable lifestyles and responsible consumption, while the Global Biofuel Alliance fosters cleaner and more sustainable energy solutions.
Raksha Mantri urged the SCO to build on the strong foundation established over the past 25 years and chart a forward-looking roadmap focused on consensus-driven cooperation and tangible outcomes. He reaffirmed India’s commitment to working closely with all Member States towards achieving these objectives. He invited Member States to participate in the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum being hosted by India later this year.
The meeting reviewed progress in multilateral economic and trade cooperation among SCO Member States and discussed measures to further strengthen cooperation in areas such as transport, finance, digital economy and social development.
The Heads of Delegation adopted the Joint Communiqué of the 25th Meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of Government, including the SCO budget for 2027, relevant financial and administrative decisions, and the PMTEC Action Plan for 2026-2030.
The SCO CHG is an important mechanism of the Organisation responsible for promoting economic and other areas of practical cooperation among Member States. India has been a full member of the SCO since 2017 and continues to participate actively in its various mechanisms.

Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 will begin in State Capital Guwahati of Assam, from tomorrow. The Mela is being organized by the Ministry of

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela will be open to public at Farm Gate, Khanapara, Guwahati, from 11 A.M. onwards till 9 O’ Clock. He said the visitors will explore the diverse range of traditional products to purchase the creations and support the artisans.

The participation of artisans from the North-Eastern States, alongside those from other parts of the country, will provide visitors with an opportunity to appreciate the diversity of India’s artistic traditions, indigenous craftsmanship and cultural heritage, he added.
He said the event aims to also encourage greater appreciation of the skills and creativity of artisans whose work contributes to preserving traditional knowledge and craft practices.

BHARAT-TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme)

It also supports the preservation and promotion of traditional arts and crafts by connecting artisans and their products with evolving consumer markets, he said.

It provides a dedicated platform for these communities to showcase their skills, market their products and strengthen their economic self-reliance through sustainable livelihood opportunities.
In addition to promoting the sale of traditional products, the Mela will help create awareness among visitors and participating communities about the welfare, financial assistance and development schemes implemented by the Ministry and its three National Corporations. The initiative seeks to complement financial and developmental support with market-oriented interventions, enabling artisans to translate their traditional skills and craftsmanship into viable livelihood opportunities, the official said.
It is pertinent to mention that through initiatives such as Shilp Samagam Mela, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to advance its efforts towards the socio-economic empowerment of disadvantaged  communities by promoting entrepreneurship, facilitating market access and supporting sustainable livelihoods.
The Mela is expected to enhance the visibility of participating artisans, expand awareness of their products and encourage greater public engagement with India’s rich handloom and handicraft traditions.

title: Wings of Change
subtitle: 10 Years of Redefining Regional Air Connectivity through UDAN
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 OCT 2026 10:17AM by PIB Delhi
content:
UDAN completes ten years in 2026. Over the past decade, it has expanded India’s regional aviation network, connecting unserved & underserved regions and improving access to air travel. Regional connectivity has supported tourism, medical access, agricultural trade and local employment, with airports such as Tezu, Deoghar and Kishangarh illustrating its impact. The launch of Modified UDAN marks the next phase of the scheme. It focuses on strengthening aviation infrastructure, ensuring operational sustainability and expanding regional air connectivity.
Connecting Regional India
Air connectivity plays an important role in regional development. It facilitates access to markets, supports tourism and expands economic opportunities. However, connecting remote and underserved areas remains important for ensuring wider access to air travel. Recognising this need, the National Civil Aviation Policy 2016 prioritised affordable
regional connectivity through financial support and infrastructure development.
In line with this objective, the
Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS),
also
known as
UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik),
was launched on
21 October 2016.
The scheme anchors its ambition on a simple yet transformative premise: making
affordable yet economically viable and profitable air travel
on regional routes.
As UDAN completes ten years, it
has expanded regional air connectivity and improved access to air travel for citizens by connecting unserved and underserved airports. A recap of the past decade reflects the rapid expansion of India’s civil aviation footprint. India is now the world’s
third-largest domestic aviation market
, with operational airports increasing from
74 in 2014 to 166 till date
. At the heart of this, transformation lies the UDAN scheme.
Building on this progress, the next phase of UDAN was launched on
4 July 2026
. The scheme now places greater emphasis on
Centre-State/UTs partnerships
. It will be complemented by a
Challenge Mode Portal for Aerodrome Development
dedicated to identifying airstrips and helipads. Together, these measures will further expand regional aviation infrastructure.
The First Decade of UDAN
UDAN entered its operational stage with the inauguration of the
first RCS-UDAN flight
from
Shimla to Delhi
in April
2017
.
Since then, the scheme has expanded regional air connectivity.
Routes Operationalised:
The scheme has operationalised 687 regional routes across India.
Aerodromes Operationalised:
A total of 95 aerodromes have been operationalised, including 17 heliports and 02 water aerodromes.
Flights Operated:
More than 3.68 lakh flights have been operated under the scheme.
Passengers Carried:
The scheme has facilitated air travel for 1.72 crore passengers.
The scheme uses market-based selection, airfare caps, concessions, and Viability Gap Funding (VGF) to encourage airline participation.
As of 15 October 2026,
Rs 5091.23 crore has been disbursed under VGF
.
Alongside expansion of civil aviation, sectoral jobs have grown from around
3 million in 2014
to nearly
7.7 million in 2026
. Additionally, it has the potential to reach 25 million by 2040.
North-Eastern Region under UDAN
Due to the difficult hilly terrain, the north-eastern states remain under-connected, which makes strengthening air connectivity an important development priority.
Under UDAN,
across the North-Eastern States,
90 priority RCS routes have been operationalised
.
52 aerodromes,
including
heliports
and
water aerodromes,
have also been
identified
in the region, of which
12 have been operationalised
.
Transitioning to Next Phase of UDAN
Since its inception, RCS-UDAN has released multiple versions of the scheme. Building on the achievements under it,
the next phase of UDAN Scheme
was formally
launched on 4 July 2026
. The scheme will be implemented in
ten years
, from
FY 2026-27 to FY 2035-36,
with a total outlay of
Rs 28,840 crore
. The focus is now on building an ecosystem towards facilitating Made in India Civil aircraft.
The scheme emphasises
affordable air travel, sustainable regional aviation operations, aerodrome development through a Challenge Mode framework, and indigenous aircraft manufacturing
.
The Modified UDAN Scheme introduces targeted measures to support sustainable growth and long-term viability of regional aviation.
Development of Aerodromes (CAPEX):
100 airports will be developed from existing unserved airstrips, with an outlay of Rs 12,159 crore over eight years. This amounts to a proposed allocation of Rs 100 crore per airport.
Operation and Maintenance (O&M) of Aerodromes:
Three years of O&M support will be provided for approximately 441 aerodromes, with an estimated outlay of Rs 2,577 crore. The financial support is capped at Rs 3.06 crore per airport per year and Rs 0.90 crore per heliport or water aerodrome per year.
Development of Modern Helipads:
200 modern helipads to be developed at an estimated cost of Rs 15 crore each. The total projected outlay is Rs 3,661 crore over eight years.
Viability Gap Funding for Airlines:
Rs 10,043 crore allocated over ten years to support airlines operating regional routes. Funding is available for up to five years, with tapered support from the third year and route exclusivity limited to three years.
Atmanirbhar Bharat and Indigenous Aviation Capacity:
An allocation of
Rs 400 crore
is proposed for two HAL Dhruv helicopters for Pawan Hans and two HAL Dornier aircraft for Alliance Air. The initiative supports indigenous aviation under Atmanirbhar Bharat and aims to strengthen connectivity in remote areas and challenging terrain.
The Next Phase Takes Shape
In the next phase of UDAN, the scheme will have a
three-pronged approach
focusing on
strengthening Centre-State/UT partnerships
,
creating aviation infrastructure
and
expanding regional air connectivity
.
Centre-State/UT Coordination:
A total of 21 MoUs were signed between the Government, participating States and Union Territories, and the Airports Authority of India (AAI). These establish a framework for coordinated identification, development and operationalisation of aviation assets. The framework will align with regional connectivity requirements and State/UT priorities.
Challenge Mode Portal for Aerodrome Development
:
The dedicated portal enables State Governments and UT Administrations to nominate airstrips and helipads for development under the next phase of UDAN. This allows States and UTs to identify locations with potential for aviation connectivity. This will facilitate the creation and upgradation of aviation infrastructure based on local requirements.
Regional Changes under UDAN
The operationalisation of regional airports under UDAN has driven socio-economic transformation across regional hubs, boosting local trade, medical access, tourism, and employment.
Purnea Airport in Bihar
Prior to 2025
, residents of the Seemanchal and Kosi regions, including Purnea, Araria, Kishanganj, Katihar, and Bhagalpur, were required
to travel over 200 km to Bagdogra Airport for air connectivity.
Journeys to major cities such as
Kolkata and Patna often involved arduous road travel of 10 hours and 8 hours, respectively
. Despite being a prominent agricultural hub known for products such as makhana, litchi, and vegetables, the region lacked direct air connectivity and air cargo facilities, constraining its economic potential. The operationalization of Purnea Airport in 2025 transformed regional connectivity by providing air
access to more than 10 districts of Bihar
.
Travel time to Kolkata has been reduced to nearly 2 hours and to Patna to about 1 hour
, significantly improving accessibility for residents, businesses, and institutions. The airport, equipped with
Bihar’s longest runway of approximately 2.8 km capable of handling A320 and B737 aircraft
, has strengthened the region’s integration with major economic centres. Furthermore, the enhanced connectivity has
stimulated local economic activity
.
Tezu Airport in Arunachal Pradesh
Situated in India’s easternmost frontier near the China border, the Lohit district of Arunachal Pradesh previously lacked air connectivity. It
forced residents to undertake journeys of over 10+ hours across 164 km to Dibrugarh or 610 km to Guwahati
for flights and medical emergencies.
Operationalised in 2021, Tezu Airport now connects over 2 lakh people
in this remote territory. The airport has
reduced travel time to Guwahati to 1 hou
r. The facility has enabled
air cargo exports for agricultural produce
such as ginger, cardamom, and rice.
Deoghar Airport in Jharkhand
Prior to July 2022
, reaching Deoghar required arduous journeys of
over 15 hours from Delhi or 7.5 hours from Kolkata by road or rail.
Pilgrims visiting
Baba Baidyanath Dham
were forced to travel more than 150 km to 200 km to reach the nearest operational airports in Ranchi or Patna. The
opening of Deoghar Airport drastically cut travel time from Delhi to just 2 hours
. Post July 2022, over
10 lakh+ pilgrims fly directly to Deoghar
annually. The airport
provides direct access for 50+ lakh devotees visiting during the peak Kanwar Yatra month
. Furthermore, the airport has
promoted
medical tourism
by facilitating patient travel to
AIIMS Deoghar
from East India. Additionally, it has boosted
local hospitality
, leading to the
establishment of over 30+ new hotels
.
Kishangarh Airport in Rajasthan
Before
direct air access in 2017
, travellers in Kishangarh, Ajmer, and Pushkar
travelled 100+ km to Jaipur
for flights. This bottleneck affected the region’s marble hub business. It also
impacted over 2 crore annual pilgrims visiting Ajmer Sharif Dargah
and
Pushkar Temple
. Post 2017, direct air cargo connectivity has enabled marble exports to Italy, the UAE, and the USA. In 2022, the airport hosted Avyanna Aviation Academy, the region’s only Category ‘A’ Flying Training Organisation (FTO). The airport
generated 200+ direct jobs
. It also spurred a
40–50% rise in local real estate values
.
The Horizon Ahead
UDAN has spent the last decade redefining India’s regional connectivity by operationalising routes and aerodromes and carrying crores of passengers. The next phase of regional aviation will depend on developing infrastructure that supports reliable and sustained operations across diverse geographies. Through the Modified UDAN Scheme, the focus extends to aerodrome development, operational support and indigenous aviation capacity. These measures seek to address the infrastructure and viability challenges of regional air travel. They aim to create a stronger foundation for connectivity across India.
